findings.message: The public tuple variant permits constructing `PreReviewGateOutcome::Blocked(Vec::new())` directly, bypassing `blocked()` validation and violating the documented non-empty invariant. Use a private or validated payload representation.
The public tuple variant permits constructing `CoverageVerifyOutcome::Blocked(Vec::new())` directly, bypassing `blocked()` validation and violating the documented non-empty invariant.

The port promises `Ok(None)` when `.commit_hash` is absent, but `FsCommitHashStore::read()` discovers Git before checking the file and returns an error when the repository cannot be discovered—even with no record present. Preserve the documented main-tip fallback by checking for absence before Git discovery, or revise the contract and callers.

The revised port explicitly abstracts `.commit_hash` filesystem access plus a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` probe. This is a technical diff-base capability required by review orchestration, not a domain invariant, so `CommitHashReader` (and its matching writer) belongs in the usecase layer rather than domain.

The gate configuration is loaded with unbounded `std::fs::read_to_string`, so a repository-authored file can cause an unbounded allocation before JSON decoding. Use the crate’s bounded-read pattern (metadata check plus capped read) and return `ReadFailed` when the size limit is exceeded.

`discover_isolated_repo_for_items_dir` returns the canonical items-directory anchor specifically so callers can verify that the discovered repository root encloses it, but this loader discards that anchor. Repository configuration such as `core.worktree` can make Git report a different root, after which both review-scope and pre-review-gate configs are loaded from that unrelated tree, potentially bypassing required gates. Preserve the anchor and fail closed unless the canonical repository root encloses it, following the existing `FsReviewScopeConfigReader::ensure_encloses` pattern.

The resolver ignores the canonical anchor returned by `discover_isolated_repo_for_items_dir` and never verifies that the discovered repository root contains the supplied `items_dir`. A Git worktree/configuration can therefore make this adapter resolve the current branch from an unrelated repository, selecting the wrong track for the gate decision. Apply the same fail-closed containment check used by the config loader before resolving the branch.

The adapter forwards `ActiveTrackResolveError::to_string()` directly into the port's `FreeText`. This exposes raw branch-derived values (for example, an arbitrary non-track branch name or invalid track slug) instead of a sanitized typed classification, violating the infrastructure boundary's sanitized-error requirement. Map detached, non-track, invalid-track, branch-read, and other failures to stable sanitized messages.

The resolver ignores the canonical anchor returned by `discover_isolated_repo_for_items_dir` and never verifies that the discovered repository root contains the supplied `items_dir`. A Git worktree/configuration can therefore make this adapter resolve the current branch from an unrelated repository, selecting the wrong track for the gate decision. Apply the same fail-closed containment check used by the config loader before resolving the branch.

The adapter forwards `ActiveTrackResolveError::to_string()` directly into `FreeText`, exposing raw branch-derived values such as arbitrary non-track branch names or invalid track slugs. Map resolution failures to stable sanitized classifications instead of propagating these values across the infrastructure boundary.

Isolated repository discovery is undone when `repo` is passed to `ActiveTrackResolveInteractor`: `SystemGitRepo`'s branch reader runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` without clearing repository-selecting variables such as `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE`. Consequently, discovery and containment can validate the `items_dir` repository while the track ID is read from a different ambient repository, dispatching the gate for the wrong track. Use an isolated branch-read path that clears repository-selection variables, and add a regression test with `GIT_DIR` targeting another repository.

The restoration inspector reads `domain-types.json` and `domain-types-baseline.json` through paths built with `join` without applying `reject_symlinks_below` or an equivalent trusted-root check. `is_file()` follows symlinks, and `std::fs::read`/`BaselineRustdocCodec::load` follow them too, so a carrier can cause evidence to be loaded from outside the repository and influence coverage eligibility.

The restoration inspector performs unbounded filesystem reads: `std::fs::read` loads the catalogue without a size limit, and `BaselineRustdocCodec::load` uses an unbounded `read_to_string` for the baseline. A repository-controlled artifact can therefore exhaust memory during the gate inspection; use bounded, symlink-safe reads before decoding.

Eligibility is returned when exactly one matching signal is source-only Red, even if additional signals for the same identity exist (for example, `[Red(found_type=false), Blue(found_type=true)]`). The signal codec permits duplicate identities, and liveness stores them in an order-dependent map, so this malformed input can make the carrier pass coverage/liveness despite contradictory evidence. Require exactly one matching signal and reject duplicate or conflicting identities.

The stateless filesystem readers still place absolute artifact paths and raw I/O diagnostics into their port errors (`path.display()` and `{e}`). The briefing requires sanitized diagnostics; these messages can disclose checkout paths and filesystem details across the infrastructure boundary. Return stable artifact/track classifications instead in `FsImplCatalogSignalReader`, `FsImplPlanReader`, and `FsTaskContractReader`.

`read_evidence_file` checks the size and regular-file status before calling `std::fs::read`, but the actual read is still unbounded and can race with replacement after the metadata check. Use an opened handle with a bounded `take(max + 1)` read (and reject overflow) so restoration inspection cannot consume arbitrary data.

The signal, impl-plan, and task-contract readers perform `symlink_metadata`/size checks and then call `std::fs::read` directly without requiring `file_type().is_file()` or using a bounded handle. A non-regular artifact such as a FIFO can block the gate, and a replacement can bypass the metadata size bound. Open and validate a regular file, then read through `take(max + 1)` with overflow detection in `FsImplCatalogSignalReader`, `FsImplPlanReader`, and `FsTaskContractReader`.

The carrier is considered eligible only when its matching Red signal has `found_type == false`. A valid baseline/current structural mismatch produces a Red signal with `found_type == true`, so legitimate source-only restoration work is incorrectly rejected as stale. Accept the exact matching Red signal regardless of `found_type`; use signal absence or a non-Red result to detect restoration.

The inspector trusts decoded signal rows without validating the document's declaration and implementation-input hashes against the current inputs. A stale signals file can therefore leave a carrier eligible after the source has already been restored, weakening the required fresh-Red/liveness check. Validate signal freshness or fail closed before classifying eligibility.

The infrastructure adapter implements the carrier eligibility policy itself, including owner uniqueness, Todo/InProgress status, overlapping attribution, and stale-signal classification. The stated architecture requires infrastructure to return typed evidence while the use-case layer owns coverage and liveness policy; keeping these decisions here bypasses that boundary and makes policy changes dependent on the adapter. Move the eligibility matrix into the use-case layer and limit this adapter to bounded evidence loading.

The codec parses the complete strict v1 DTO before checking `schema_version`. Future-version documents can therefore fail on v1-specific shape/validation before the unsupported-version guard, violating the required fail-closed envelope-first schema handling. Parse a minimal version envelope first, reject unsupported versions, then deserialize the strict DTO.

`resolve_items_dir_under_current_repo` constructs raw `io::Error` messages containing absolute repository and `items_dir` paths, and callers propagate `e` directly into operator-facing errors. This bypasses the scope’s sanitized-diagnostics boundary and can disclose local checkout paths; return a sanitized classification/typed error instead.

`resolve_items_dir_under_current_repo` discovers the repository with `SystemGitRepo::discover()`, which inherits the ambient Git environment and process working directory, instead of anchoring discovery to the supplied `items_dir`. A `GIT_DIR`/worktree override can therefore make readers resolve and inspect a different repository than the requested items tree, bypassing the intended trusted-root isolation. Use isolated discovery from the supplied path and verify the discovered root encloses it.

`resolve_items_dir_under_current_repo` still calls `SystemGitRepo::discover()`, which uses the process CWD and ambient repository-selection variables such as `GIT_DIR`. With a relative `items_dir`, readers can resolve against a different repository than the supplied items tree, undermining the trusted-root/gate decision boundary. Discover in isolation from the supplied `items_dir` and verify containment.

`discover_from_isolated` validates the requested repository, but `repo.current_branch()` subsequently runs Git without clearing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`. Ambient repository-selection variables can therefore redirect the branch read to another repository after containment succeeds, resolving the wrong track for pre-review dispatch. Use an isolated branch-read path and add a cross-repository environment regression test.

After the direct child exits or is killed, the runner unconditionally joins both pipe-reader threads. A descendant that inherited stdout or stderr can keep either pipe open, causing `run` to block indefinitely past its configured timeout; `child.kill()` only terminates the direct PID. Spawn commands in a process group and bound output collection/terminate the whole group, following the existing bounded Git runner pattern.

`thread::spawn` panics when the OS cannot create an output-reader thread. This is production library adapter code, and the panic also abandons an already-spawned child process. Use `thread::Builder::spawn`, map failure to `ProgramRunnerError`, and terminate/reap the child on reader-start failure.

The loader deserializes the complete strict v1 DTO before validating `schema_version`. A future-version document whose payload shape changed will therefore be reported as malformed JSON instead of an unsupported schema version. Deserialize a minimal version envelope first, reject unsupported versions, and only then decode the strict version-specific DTO.

A reader can discover that stdout exceeded the limit just after `wait_for_completion` observes the child exit. The returned `stdout.exceeded` value is not added to `cleanup_after_termination`, so the runner waits on stderr without terminating surviving descendants; it may eventually return `TimedOut` instead of `OutputLimitExceeded`. Treat a reader-reported overflow as an immediate reason to terminate the process group before collecting the other stream.

Post-spawn failures are propagated directly with `?`. If waiting or receiving a pipe result fails, the function returns without terminating/reaping the child process group or joining the remaining reader. Route every error after a successful spawn through the same bounded cleanup path before returning it.

This addition pushes the production portion of the module to 703 lines, exceeding the repository's configured maximum of 700; `bin/sotp verify module-size` now fails for this file. Split production responsibilities so the module remains within the enforced boundary.

`reject_symlinks_up_to_root` is propagated directly even though its error payload renders the rejected path. Callers that report this error therefore expose absolute checkout components for a symlinked `items_dir`, contradicting the required sanitized-diagnostics boundary. Convert guard and canonicalization failures to `sanitized_io_error(io_classification(...))` before returning them.

Late output-limit detection does not reliably terminate the process group. When stdout exceeded its limit after the leader exited, `receive_after_reader_overflow` skips termination whenever stderr has already completed; a late stderr overflow never triggers termination at all. Background descendants with redirected streams can consequently survive an `OutputLimitExceeded` result. Terminate and reap the group unconditionally whenever either reader reports `exceeded`, then collect the remaining reader boundedly.

Domain identifier validation now runs inside serde deserializers and maps failures through `serde::de::Error::custom`. Valid JSON containing an invalid task ID, track ID, layer, or entry key therefore returns `TaskContractCodecError::Json` instead of the documented `Validation` variant; because `TaskContractDocument::new` cannot currently fail, `Validation` is effectively unreachable. Preserve strict raw DTO decoding, then perform domain conversions in `decode` and map `ValidationError` to the typed validation error.

`cleanup_deadline` starts when reader collection begins, not when termination occurs. If the command leader exits while a descendant holds a pipe, collection can consume the full command timeout before terminating the process group; the code then switches to a cleanup deadline that expired long ago and can immediately return `WaitFailed` instead of the required `TimedOut` or `OutputLimitExceeded` outcome. Start the cleanup grace period when `cleanup_after_termination` transitions to true.

Late overflow handling invokes a non-idempotent process-group terminator after `wait_for_completion` may already have reaped the leader. If a short-lived command exceeds the output cap between the overflow-channel poll and `try_wait`, an otherwise empty process group makes the kill command fail, causing `TerminateFailed` instead of the required `OutputLimitExceeded` outcome. Treat an already-empty/reaped group as successful cleanup while still terminating any surviving descendants.

`terminate_for_reader_overflow` still treats an already-empty process group as a termination failure. Deferring `child.wait()` does not keep the group alive: after a finite command exceeds the output cap and exits, its leader can remain a zombie while the process group is empty, causing `terminate_bounded_git_child` to fail and return `TerminateFailed` instead of the required `OutputLimitExceeded`. Treat empty-group cleanup as successful after reaping the child, while still terminating groups containing descendants.

`process_group_exists` treats every non-zero `kill -0` result as proof that the group is absent. `kill -0` also fails with `EPERM` when a group still exists but cannot be signalled, such as when a configured command leaves a privilege-changing descendant. The caller then masks the failed SIGKILL as successful after reaping the leader, and pipe-reader joins can block indefinitely on that surviving descendant. Distinguish `ESRCH` from permission and other failures, suppressing only the former.

Timeout checks occur only while waiting for pipe-reader results. A child can close or redirect both stdout and stderr and continue running (for example, `sh -c 'exec >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 60'`); both readers then complete immediately and this unconditional `child.wait()` blocks beyond `invocation.timeout`. Use deadline-aware child polling and termination after the readers complete.

The cleanup path discards the `recv_timeout` result and then unconditionally joins the reader. If the second reader fails to spawn while a descendant outside the killed process group retains the first pipe, the cleanup deadline expires but `join_reader` can block indefinitely. Only join after receiving completion; return a cleanup error on timeout.

`test_loader_rejects_persisted_host_argument_as_invalid_config` only covers the split `--host codex` spelling. The adapter preserves arguments verbatim, while downstream validation rejects only an argument exactly equal to `--host`; therefore `--host=codex` is accepted even though Clap treats it as the same option. This lets operator-owned configuration persist a provider host, bypassing fail-closed validation. Reject the `--host=` form and add a loader regression case.

`PHASE_COMMANDS_CONFIG` points to `.harness/config/phase-commands.json`, but neither the current worktree nor HEAD contains that file. Consequently the production `FsPhaseCommandConfigLoader` always returns `ReadFailed` for the repository, breaking every `phase validate`, `phase explain`, and `phase enter` operation; the temporary-file unit tests do not catch this deployment gap. Ship the configuration at this path or point the adapter at the actual operator-owned config.

The chain-specific path reimplements check-approved via `results_core`, whose lookup selects only the first origin-matching cache entry. Unlike the normal interactor, it does not fail closed when duplicate matching entries include a non-Pass verdict. A duplicate Pass/Fail cache pair can therefore make `--chain 1` or `--chain 2` incorrectly return `AllApproved`.

Chain-1 approval is not isolated from Chain 2. Delegating to `results_core` invokes `resolve_chain1_only_scope`, which reads `architecture-rules.json` and rejects malformed rules or catalogue-without-spec states before enumerating Chain 1. Consequently, a fully approved Chain 1 can fail solely because Chain 2 is unenumerable, contrary to the selected-chain contract. Enumerate the selected scope directly or move filtering into the approval interactor.

The gate evaluates two different cache snapshots. `results_core` first reads the cache to classify a record as Pass, then this loop rereads it and only checks for non-Pass entries. If the cache is removed or atomically replaced with an empty document between reads, the empty second result passes `any`, while the earlier `total_pass` still produces `AllApproved`. Load each selected cache scope once and decide missing/non-Pass status from that stable snapshot.

The added selected-chain approval branch increases the production portion of this module from 653 to 725 lines, exceeding the repository's 700-line maximum. Extract this gate logic into a focused adapter/helper module; test code beginning after the production section is exempt, but these lines are not.

The selected Chain2 approval path can return `NoPairs` for a nonexistent track. `load_chain2_pairs` only inspects declared catalogues; when `architecture-rules.json` is absent or all catalogues are absent, it never invokes the pair source (which validates the track directory), so an invalid `track_id` is treated as a vacuous pass. This bypasses the approval gate's fail-closed invalid-track behavior.

`load_results_tddd_bindings` treats a missing `architecture-rules.json` as an empty binding set. On this gate path, `--chain 2` then enumerates no scopes and returns `NoPairs`, which the driver renders as success. Because this configuration determines which selected-chain pairs must be approved, missing configuration must fail closed rather than reuse the informational-results fallback.

The selected Chain-2 path omits the resolver's catalogue-before-spec ordering check. If a declared catalogue exists while `spec.json` is absent but the catalogue is empty or has no spec refs, pair enumeration returns zero pairs and the gate succeeds as `NoPairs`. Reject `spec.json` absence whenever any selected Chain-2 catalogue is present, using the same symlink-aware preflight as `RefVerifyScopeResolver`.

The selected path reimplements approval policy inside infrastructure: production-pair filtering, scope grouping, full-key matching, and Pass/non-Pass outcome classification duplicate `RefVerifyCheckApprovedInteractor`, while the All path still uses that use-case service. This creates two gate implementations that can drift and places business rules outside the use-case layer. Express chain selection in the use-case command/interactor and keep this module limited to I/O adaptation.

`spec_exists` accepts any non-symlink filesystem entry, including a directory or device, as a valid `spec.json`. With a valid but empty catalogue, pair enumeration never reads the spec and returns zero pairs, so `check-approved --chain 2` reports `NoPairs` instead of rejecting the invalid artifact. Require `spec.json` to be a regular file (and preferably decode it) before this early return.

These 59 production lines move the test boundary to line 733, leaving 732 production lines in the module. This exceeds the repository's 700-line production-module maximum and defeats the module's stated extraction boundary; move the selected-approval helpers into `selected_check_approved.rs` or another focused module.

`items_dir_abs` is canonicalized but symlinks are never rejected before `track_dir` and `metadata.json` are read. A symlinked `items_dir` can redirect this gate to another in-repository directory, while `load_base_branch` treats that symlinked path as its trusted root. Reject symlinks at the input boundary (using the existing up-to-root guard) before canonicalization.

An error reading `.commit_hash`—including symlink detection, malformed content, permission errors, or other I/O failures—is converted into a warning and silently replaced with the configured base branch. Because this base determines the diff used for the review verdict, fallback can evaluate a different scope and is not fail-closed; propagate the read error, reserving fallback for an explicitly absent file.

The repository CWD is restored immediately after resolving the base, but `cycle.get_review_states()` invokes `GitDiffGetter`, which discovers its repository from the ambient process CWD. When `--items-dir` targets a repository different from the invocation directory, the persisted review state is computed from the wrong repository (or fails), defeating the trusted-root check. Keep the entire diff/state evaluation anchored to `canonical_root`, or inject a root-bound diff adapter.

`with_repository_cwd` mutates process-global CWD. The port is `Send + Sync`, so concurrent state checks can observe each other’s temporary directories; one call can discover or diff the other call’s repository and restoration can race as well. Avoid process-global CWD mutation by making the git/diff adapters explicitly repository-rooted (or serialize the whole operation with a process-wide guard).

The non-Unix implementation only rejects a symlink at the leaf and then calls `File::open`, so symlinked parent directories can redirect reads outside the repository. `verify_fd_within_root` is also a no-op on non-Unix platforms. Apply an equivalent boundary/root verification on every supported platform and fail closed when verification is unavailable.

The rooted review adapters still execute gate-defining Git commands through `SystemGitRepo::output`/`discover_from`, which use `guarded_git_command()` without removing repository-selecting environment variables or disabling replace/graft history rewrites. `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, replacement refs, or grafts can therefore make diff/base results come from a different or synthetic history despite the rooted path. Use the existing isolated Git command path for discovery, base resolution, ancestry, and diff reads.

On non-Unix platforms, the file is opened before `verify_scope_path_within_root` canonicalizes the pathname. A concurrent replacement of a parent/leaf symlink between those operations can leave the already-open handle referring outside the trusted root while the later pathname check passes. The platform-specific verifier must bind the opened handle to the trusted root, or fail closed when that cannot be done.

`resolve_diff_base` still uses `SystemGitRepo::output` for the branch fallback. That command inherits repository-selecting environment variables and history-rewrite inputs, so a gate-defining base can be resolved from `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or altered history even though the subsequent diff getter uses the isolated lane. Resolve the base through the same isolated, bounded Git command path and apply the same history-rewrite protections.

On non-Unix platforms, containment is checked before opening the file, but the pathname can be swapped between `verify_scope_path_within_root` and `open_nofollow_read`; the opened handle can then refer outside the trusted root while the check has already passed. Use a platform handle-based containment check, or fail closed on platforms without one.

On Unix systems without `/proc` (notably macOS and FreeBSD), containment falls back to canonicalizing the pathname after the file has already been opened. A concurrent symlink/path swap can make the opened descriptor refer outside the trusted root while the post-open pathname check passes. Fail closed when handle containment cannot be verified, or use a platform-specific descriptor verification mechanism.

The hasher loads every changed regular file into an unbounded `Vec` via `read_to_end`. A large tracked or untracked file can exhaust memory during this gate check. Hash incrementally from the file or enforce a bounded input size and return an adapter error when exceeded.

The Unix hasher now requires `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` for every file and returns an error when that path cannot be read. macOS and FreeBSD commonly lack `/proc`, so every non-empty review hash fails and the check-zero-findings operation cannot evaluate review state on those supported Unix targets. Use a platform-specific descriptor containment mechanism or explicitly gate/support the platform instead of unconditionally requiring Linux’s `/proc`.

The `.commit_hash` ancestry check is delegated through `FsCommitHashStore::read()`, which discovers and invokes Git using the ambient process environment rather than the isolated `git` handle used for the rest of this adapter. Repository-selecting variables or history rewrites can therefore validate a persisted base against a different/synthetic repository before its hash is used for the gate diff. Perform ancestry validation through the same isolated Git lane rooted at `git.root()`, or reject the stored hash unless validation is performed against that exact repository/history.

Git path output is parsed as newline-delimited, lossy UTF-8 even though `--name-only` may quote non-ASCII/control-character filenames. The resulting value is not the real repository path, so it can be misclassified and hashed as `DELETED`; subsequent content changes then leave the review hash unchanged. Use `-z`, parse NUL-delimited paths, and reject unsupported non-UTF-8 names fail-closed.

The review manifest hashes only each path and its contents, omitting Git-tracked file mode. Toggling the executable bit on a file already in the diff leaves the target paths and content unchanged, so a stored `zero_findings` hash remains current for a semantically different artifact. Include tracked mode/type in the canonical hash encoding.

The metadata `base_branch` is only non-empty, but it is passed directly to `git rev-parse`, which accepts arbitrary revision expressions and tags such as `HEAD~1`. When `.commit_hash` is absent, this can move the merge base and omit committed files from the review target. Validate with `check-ref-format --branch` and resolve `refs/heads/<name>^{commit}` using `--end-of-options`, following `dry_check/diff_base_resolver.rs`.

`read_for_git` collapses every unsuccessful ancestry probe—including Git spawn failure, timeout/output-limit failure, and other I/O errors—into `Ok(None)`. `check_zero_findings` then falls back to `base_branch`, which can change the measured diff rather than fail closed. Distinguish a normal non-ancestor exit from adapter/I/O errors and propagate the latter as an error; likewise avoid converting isolated discovery failures to `None` in the legacy reader.

For a relative `items_dir`, repository discovery starts at the supplied path but the adapter then discards that canonical anchor and rebuilds the path as `git.root().join(items_dir)`. A crafted `core.worktree` can make Git report another root, causing validation and review-state reads to switch trees. Use `discover_isolated_repo_for_items_dir` and enforce the same anchor containment check as `FsReviewScopeConfigReader::ensure_encloses`.

After decoding `metadata.json`, the adapter does not verify that the document's track ID equals the requested directory/`track_id`. A copied or mismatched metadata document can therefore supply another track's base branch and change the gate-defining diff. Reject this identity mismatch before using the snapshot.

`metadata.json` is loaded with unbounded `read_to_string` after only a symlink check. A repository-controlled oversized file can exhaust memory, and a FIFO can block the gate indefinitely. Require a bounded regular-file read, following the existing bounded track-artifact patterns.

The supposed Git-mode normalization treats any execute bit as executable. Git tracks the owner execute bit, so changing a file from `0755` to `0655` changes Git mode from `100755` to `100644` while this function still returns `100755`; the review hash can remain current across a semantic mode change. Test `filesystem_mode & 0o100` instead.

`open_nofollow_read` opens a diff path before proving it is regular and does not use `O_NONBLOCK`. An untracked FIFO—or a regular file replaced by one after diff enumeration—blocks in `open()` before the post-open metadata check. Open nonblocking and then reject non-regular descriptors.

`reject_symlinks_below` does not prove that `self.path` is actually beneath `trusted_root`; an outside path with no symlinks passes and can subsequently be read, created, or removed. Establish canonical containment before the guard, following `dry_check/commit_hash_store.rs::locate_record`.

The commit record is read with unbounded `read_to_string` and without requiring a regular file. A large `.commit_hash` can exhaust memory and a FIFO can block indefinitely. Reuse the bounded regular-file approach in `dry_check/commit_hash_store.rs::read_bounded_record`.

`read_bounded_regular_file` performs `symlink_metadata`/regular-file checks and then calls `File::open` separately. A concurrent replacement can turn the checked path into a symlink or FIFO: the read may follow an external file or block indefinitely, despite the caller’s symlink guard and pre-open FIFO defense. Open atomically with no-follow/nonblocking flags where supported, then validate the opened handle and fail closed on unsupported platforms.

`read_bounded_regular_file` still separates `symlink_metadata`/regular-file validation from `File::open`. A concurrent replacement can turn the path into a symlink or FIFO after validation, causing an external read or blocking the gate. Open atomically with no-follow/nonblocking semantics where supported, validate the opened handle, and fail closed when this cannot be guaranteed.

The shared trusted-file reader is compiled for all Unix targets, but `verify_opened_file_within_root` is implemented only for Linux; on macOS it always returns `Unsupported`. Consequently, any existing `.commit_hash` record causes dry-check and review-state reads to fail on macOS, despite the hasher explicitly supporting macOS. Implement Darwin descriptor containment (such as `F_GETPATH`) or exclude macOS consistently.

`locate_record` validates a missing relative parent as though it were rooted beneath `canonical_root`, but callers continue performing I/O with the original CWD-relative path. For example, with trusted root `/repo`, CWD `/tmp`, and `new/.commit_hash`, this returns `NoParent`, after which `FsCommitHashStore::write` creates `/tmp/new/.commit_hash` outside the trusted root. Reject relative record paths or return and consistently use an anchored absolute path.

The macOS implementation uses direct `unsafe` blocks even though the crate root declares `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so the infrastructure crate cannot compile on macOS. The duplicate macOS test helper in `review_v2/hasher.rs` has the same problem. Use a safe descriptor-path abstraction or fail closed without compiling unsafe code.

Symlink errors are misclassified in both directions: this unconditional mapping turns a genuine symlink rejection from `locate_record` into `CommitHashError::Io`, while `reject_symlinks` classifies every `InvalidInput` error (including malformed paths such as an interior NUL) as `SymlinkDetected`. Use the guard's `is_symlink_rejection` marker consistently so the port's error taxonomy remains accurate.

The exported `GitDiffGetter` still executes every Git query through `SystemGitRepo::output`, which uses unbounded `Command::output()` and has no execution deadline. The main review compositions use this adapter, so a pathological Git process or sufficiently large path set can hang the gate or exhaust memory. Route this path through a bounded runner as well as the new rooted adapter.

The fixed-size buffer bounds per-read memory but not total bytes or execution time. A very large regular file—or one continuously appended while being hashed—can keep this loop running indefinitely and block the review gate. Enforce a configured total-byte bound or otherwise guarantee a bounded, stable input snapshot.

The new document loader uses `is_file()` and `read_to_string()`, both of which follow symlinks. A symlinked workflow document can therefore point outside the repository or replace the checked content, allowing this architecture gate to be bypassed. Reject symlinks with `symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` before reading.

`read_to_string` loads each workflow document without a size limit. A large repository-controlled document can cause excessive memory use or OOM during verification; use a bounded read consistent with the infrastructure loader pattern.

The regression gate matches only exact single-space substrings. A valid direct dispatch such as `bin/sotp capability  exec spec-designer` (or one containing tabs/line continuations) is still interpreted as the forbidden writer command but passes this check, allowing the phase-entry gates to be bypassed. Tokenize or normalize command whitespace and add bypass-case tests.

The prose regression patterns do not match the actual pre-change launch wording in the canonical harness workflows. They are lowercase and require `invoke` to be immediately followed by the backticked writer, so strings such as `Invoke the `spec-designer` capability` and `Invoke spec-designer capability` pass this check. Restoring those direct launch instructions would therefore bypass the AC-15 gate. Normalize case and cover the original optional article/backtick forms with tests.

The prose detector treats every `invoke <writer>` phrase as a forbidden dispatch, including explicit prohibitions such as “Do not invoke the `spec-designer` directly; use phase entry.” That makes the architecture gate reject valid documentation explaining the required rule. Because `architecture-rules.json` permits `cli` to depend only on `cli_driver`, the caller cannot construct the named selection without a forbidden dependency or an undeclared public API. Consequently, no declared layer owns AC-18's invalid-scope rejection and omission-to-`All` conversion. Add a cli_driver-accessible raw-value constructor/selector and assign validation to exactly one layer.

The membership check is not exhaustive over `PreReviewGateKind`. If another valid gate variant is added, a matrix containing only that gate will return `NotApplicable`; if combined with `TaskContractLiveness`, the new gate will be silently skipped. This violates the dispatcher's fail-closed/no-silent-skip contract. Iterate over the configured gates with an exhaustive `match`, or return a typed error for unsupported combinations.

`ReviewTrackSelector::Explicit` is exercised only with a resolver that succeeds with the same track ID, so the tests do not prove that explicit IDs bypass current-branch resolution. A regression that always invokes the resolver would still pass but would break explicit review on a non-track branch. Add a test using `FailingCurrentTrackResolver` with an explicit selector and assert dispatch succeeds without resolver use.

The new public `ReviewScopeSelector::Other` dispatch path has no test; every command in the suite uses `Named`. Consequently, the catch-all scope conversion and matrix lookup could regress without detection. Add a dispatch test backed by a `ScopeName::Other` matrix entry and verify the expected applicable or not-applicable outcome.

`CoverageVerifyInteractor::verify_coverage` discards the caller/composition-selected items root and always passes `Path::new("track/items")` to every reader and the restoration inspector. Any direct adapter or alternate composition that honors the port's `items_dir` argument will inspect the wrong track artifacts, so coverage results can be incorrect. Carry the selected items directory through `CoverageVerifyCommand` (or an equivalent injected usecase context) instead of hardcoding it.

`TaskStatusAttributor::load` similarly hardcodes `track/items` when invoking the newly path-aware task-contract and impl-plan ports. The status-lane summaries used by test-obligation check/results therefore ignore the actual artifact root and can attribute statuses from a different workspace when a reader honors its `items_dir` argument. Pass the selected items directory through this helper and its callers.

The new public `PreReviewGatedReviewInteractor` has no tests in the reviewed usecase scope for successful delegation, gate-blocked execution, resolver/config errors, or ensuring the inner reviewer is not invoked after a failed gate. This leaves the central aggregate decorator's fail-closed orchestration and all three launch paths unverified.

`CoverageVerifyInteractor::verify_coverage` hardcodes `Path::new("track/items")` instead of receiving the command-selected items directory. Direct adapters that honor the path-aware reader ports will inspect the wrong track artifacts, producing incorrect coverage results.

`TaskStatusAttributor::load` hardcodes `track/items` when invoking the path-aware task-contract and impl-plan ports. Status-lane attribution can therefore read artifacts from a different workspace instead of the selected root; the items directory must be carried through this helper and its callers.

Source-only carrier eligibility remains delegated to `SourceOnlyBaselineRestorationInspectorPort::inspect`, whose contract returns the final `Eligible`/`Ineligible` policy decision. The cross-scope handoff requires usecase-owned eligibility policy with infrastructure supplying bounded typed evidence; this usecase currently only forwards the adapter's decision into a coverage violation.

The new public `PreReviewGatedReviewInteractor` has no tests covering successful delegation, gate-blocked execution, resolver/config errors, or the three launch paths. The aggregate decorator's fail-closed orchestration and prevention of inner-service invocation after a failed gate are therefore unverified.

The pre-review dispatcher drops the caller's `items_dir`: `PreReviewCommandDispatchCommand` carries only `repository_root`, and each `ProgramInvocation` supplies no `--items-dir`. With a non-default items directory, configured task-contract commands inspect `track/items` instead of the requested directory, so the gate can evaluate the wrong artifacts.

Recursive invocation protection is bypassable because it denies only the exact executable token `bin/sotp`. A configured relative command such as `./bin/sotp review local` (or `bin/./sotp review local`) passes validation and recursively re-enters the gated review service, defeating the guard and potentially exhausting processes.

The dispatcher appends `--items-dir <path>` to every configured command. The configured `signal calc-impl-catalog` and `signal check-impl-catalog` subcommands do not accept that flag, so every scope using these commands fails at CLI argument parsing before the pre-review gate runs.

The gated review still drops `items_dir`: `PreReviewCommandDispatchCommand` carries only `repository_root`, and the command invocation forwards only the configured argv. Consequently, when review is invoked with a non-default `items_dir`, pre-review commands fall back to each CLI's default `track/items` and evaluate the wrong artifacts.

`ReadyForReview` and `Blocked` both carry unrestricted `ProgramExecutionRecord` values. A `PreReviewCommandDispatchService` implementation can therefore return `ReadyForReview` containing a timeout or non-zero exit, and the decorator will start the reviewer without rechecking it. Use success/failure-refined record types so the authorization state cannot represent failed commands.

The outcome migration weakened the negative liveness and coverage tests to merely assert `outcome != Passed`. These tests now succeed if the interactor emits the wrong violation variant, entry, signal, or count—for example, the NonBlueSignal test would accept MissingTaskContract. Destructure `Blocked(NonEmptyVec)` and restore the exact payload assertions throughout these cases.

The dispatch tests exercise only zero and non-zero `Exited` outcomes; neither `TimedOut` nor `OutputLimitExceeded` is tested through the dispatcher. Add cases proving both outcomes block review and prevent later configured commands from running, as required by the bounded execution contract.

The explicit track fail-closed guard was removed: `ReviewTrackSelector::Explicit(track_id)` now bypasses branch resolution, allowing gates to run for a track different from the current branch. This violates the briefing’s dispatcher contract and permits wrong-track gating.

`PhaseCommandConfig::try_new` does not inspect writer or pre-entry argv for a persisted `--host`. For example, a configured `bin/sotp capability exec … --host claude` command is accepted, allowing the validated operator-owned configuration to hard-code caller identity. This violates IN-11/AC-13 and can cause later dispatch to choose behavior based on configuration rather than the runtime caller. Reject host-bearing phase commands during configuration validation and cover both writer and pre-entry cases.

The persisted-host check only rejects an argument exactly equal to `--host`. The public `capability exec` CLI also accepts the standard `--host=claude` form, so a configured command containing that token still passes construction and configuration loading. This allows operator-owned configuration to persist provider identity despite IN-11/AC-13. Reject the `--host=<value>` form as well and add regression coverage.

`host` を付与した writer の実行時 argv が outcome の execution record に反映されません。`run` は `ProgramInvocation` には `writer_argv(...)` を渡しますが、`ProgramExecutionRecord.command` には元の `ConfiguredCommand` を保存するため、`PhaseCommandEnterOutcome::Completed` / `Blocked` から監査すると `--host <provider>` が欠落します。AC-03 の展開済み argv の監査要件を満たせず、実際に起動したコマンドを再現できません。実行時 argv を記録するか、host 付与済みの command record を生成してください。

`CheckZeroFindingsBuildFn` injects the entire application operation as an opaque `Fn`, and the interactor only forwards to it. The production evaluator behind this generic builds the review runtime, reads the filesystem-backed `review.json`, and performs the fail-closed `ReviewState` mapping in `cli_composition`; this bypasses an explicit usecase-owned secondary port and lets infrastructure/application logic escape `usecase-purity` scanning. Inject a state-reader/resolver port and perform the `ReviewState` → `ReviewCheckZeroFindingsOutcome` orchestration in this interactor.

`CheckZeroFindingsBuildFn` injects the complete application operation as an opaque `F: Fn`, leaving the interactor as a pass-through. Its production function builds the review runtime, accesses the filesystem-backed review store plus diff/hash adapters, and maps `ReviewState` to the command outcome in `cli_composition`; the generic indirection hides that runtime dependency from `usecase-purity`. Replace it with explicit usecase-owned secondary ports and keep the fail-closed state-to-outcome orchestration in this interactor.

`ScopeName` sentinel classification is business logic implemented in the usecase via `eq_ignore_ascii_case("other")`. Deciding which domain enum variant a raw scope denotes belongs on `domain::review_v2::ScopeName`; keeping it here duplicates `MainScopeName`'s reserved-name rule and risks inconsistent parsing across usecases. Add a domain-owned parser/constructor and only map its error here.

Raw scope classification still branches in the usecase instead of delegating to the domain-owned `ScopeName::parse`. This duplicates `ScopeName` business rules and is already behaviorally inconsistent: the domain parser classifies case-insensitive `"Other"` as `ScopeName::Other`, while this path rejects it through `MainScopeName::new`. Parse through `ScopeName` here, then map the resulting variant to `ReviewScopeSelector`.

The gate now accepts case-insensitive `Other` via `ScopeName::parse`, but forwards the original `group` string unchanged to `inner.run_local`. The real composition path recognizes only the exact lowercase `other` sentinel and otherwise attempts to construct a main scope, so `--group Other` passes the pre-review commands and then fails during the actual review instead of consistently reviewing the `Other` scope. Normalize the forwarded group or preserve the downstream sentinel contract.

Changing the reviewer default to 3,600 seconds leaves the canonical review-fix invocation budget stale: `.harness/capabilities/review-fix-lead.md:103-109` still prescribes 16,320,000 ms, calculated from four 3,600-second gates, a 1,800-second reviewer, and 120 seconds overhead. With this default, a worst-case invocation needs 18,120,000 ms, so the shell tool can kill a legitimate reviewer about 30 minutes early and record no round. Update the capability budget/instructions and callers for the new default, or retain 1,800 seconds.

Host-default selection is implemented as a branching decision in the binary layer. The CLI should preserve the optional host in the typed input and dispatch it; the already wired `CapabilityDriver` should apply its `default_host`. Keeping `unwrap_or_else` here violates the CLI thin-bin contract by placing application policy in `apps/cli`.

Driver-construction errors are printed verbatim. `capability_driver()` forwards `AgentProfilesError` text, whose I/O and trusted-root variants contain absolute repository/config paths, so this newly reachable failure path exposes internal filesystem details despite the sanitized-diagnostics requirement. Convert it to a stable public diagnostic before writing to stderr.
`CapabilityExecDriverInput.host` は `ProviderNameArg` なのに、`args.host` の `Option<ProviderNameArg>` をそのまま代入しているため、CLI crate がコンパイルできません。省略時の host を composition/driver のデフォルトで解決してから入力を構築する必要があります。

This retirement test does not actually verify that the provider-specific subcommands were removed: both former commands required several arguments, so `try_parse_from(["sotp", command])` already returned an error before this change due to missing required arguments. The test would therefore stay green if either variant were accidentally restored. Parse a formerly valid complete invocation and assert that it now fails as an unknown subcommand (or assert the specific clap error kind).
This does not compile: `args.chain` is moved while `args` is borrowed, but `RefVerifyCheckChainArg` is not `Copy`. Match on `&args.chain` (or derive `Copy`).

`CheckZeroFindingsArgs` is not registered in `ReviewCommand` and has no execution path, so `review check-zero-findings` cannot be invoked; the added tests only exercise an artificial standalone parser and do not cover the actual CLI.

[P1] Serialize process-wide CWD mutation with a crate-wide lock. These new enum-route tests change the process CWD while holding `env_lock()`, but that lock is private to this module; other tests in the same CLI unit-test binary mutate CWD under different locks (for example `commands/git.rs::cwd_lock` and `track::test_support::process_env_lock`). The template smoke runs `cargo test --all-features`, whose parallel libtest execution can therefore switch or restore CWD while this test is running, making git discovery target another temporary repository and causing flaky failures. Use one shared lock for all CWD/environment-mutating CLI tests or move these cases to process-isolated integration tests.

The fixture is a Rust raw string, so `\\n` reaches `/bin/sh` unchanged and `printf` emits the literal characters `\n`, not a newline. Both new matrix tests compare `phase-audit.txt` against real newline-separated records and therefore fail. Use `printf '%s\n'` in the raw string.

D4 embeds workflow procedure rather than only recording the lifecycle decision: stopping the task, having impl-planner edit both artifacts, rerunning named checks, and sequencing implementation review are downstream workflow/capability details. Removing lines 88–91 would preserve the decision that a restored carrier must become stale and be removed before settlement; delegate this procedure to the applicable workflow SSoT.

The Validation Strategy is an operational test matrix with fixture cases, round-trip checks, and named gate assertions. Removing lines 128–139 leaves D1–D4 unchanged, so this detail obscures the recorded decisions and belongs in the implementation/test contract rather than the ADR.

`ScopeName` の検証は空文字・非 ASCII・予約名などの形式だけを検査し、構成に存在しない `nonexistent` のような名前も受理する。そのため `Named(validated ScopeName)` だけでは、Context・理由・Rejected Alternative C が決定事項として主張する「未知 scope を fail-closed で拒否する」を実現できない。D1 に scope universe への membership 検証と未知名の拒否を明記する必要がある。
